stories.headline: India's World Cup dream over: How late errors ended men's hockey team's semi-final hopes
stories.title: India's World Cup dream over: How late errors ended men's hockey team's semi-final hopes
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The match began with India executing a disciplined and composed defensive plan, successfully keeping the hosts at bay during the opening half.

Amstelveen: The Indian men's hockey team have crashed out of the semi-final race of the FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 after conceding two late goals in the final quarter against reigning Olympic champions the Netherlands today.
Despite a flawless and composed first half, a series of unforced errors in the final ten minutes saw India suffer a 1-3 defeat at the Wagener Stadium this evening.
India entered the must-win fixture knowing that only a victory would keep their hopes of a podium finish alive.
Instead, the defeat leaves them pointless in the second round.
This means Monday's upcoming clash against Argentina is now entirely inconsequential.
Even if they win on Monday, they will only have three points, which is mathematically insufficient to reach the last four.
The men in blue have never beaten the Netherlands in World Cup history.
In fact, the closest they came was in the 1973 World Cup final, which the Dutch won in a penalty shootout.
The Indian backline made no mistakes.
They did not let the Dutch midfield keep the ball for long.
